To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cyanobacterion Phormidium allocates its internal resources in a proportional manner during prolonged darkness.
prolonged darkness induced a proportional decrease in the cell composition of Phormidium, which was maintained at a constant ratio throughout the whole incubations.

the cell composition of Phormidium cells remained constant throughout the whole incubating period, and that this homeostasis of cell constituents was achieved by a proportional decrease in all major cellular constituents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the homeostasis of cell chemical composition in relation to the availability of resources in the environment, a key aspect of the ecology of organisms in general.
the homeostasis of the cell composition in cyanobacteria and the possible role of homeostasis in the evolution of the cell.
the study of the chemical composition of organisms and the way in which it changes in response to environmental factors.

the cell composition is homeostatic and that the cell composition of the cells is homeostatic.
homeostasis of cell components during prolonged darkness is a result of the balance between the energy and nutrient availability and the energy requirements of the cell.
homeostasis is a strategy that allows organisms to maintain their cell composition and, therefore, their physiological state during periods of environmental change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Phormidium has a homeostatic strategy to cope with environmental changes, which involves the maintenance of balanced ratios of the major cellular constituents.
the cyanobacterial cells are able to respond to environmental changes in a homeostatically way.

Phormidium cells are able to allocate resources in a homeo- static way in response to environmental changes, and that the maintenance of balanced cellular composition (homeostatic cell composition) is an evolutionary strategy related with environmental changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell composition of Phormidium is not fixed, but it can be modified to maintain homeostasis in response to environmental changes.

the homeostasis of cell constituents in response to prolonged light/dark cycles is not only an adaptation of photosynthetic organisms to the light/dark cycle of the environment, but also an adaptation to the availability of resources.
